description: Ceiling for the kasirmu-core production line count (Phase 3 P3.4, plan section 11.1). scripts/verify-core-size.py fails when the measured count rises above ceiling. Lowering it is a deliberate edit, exactly as a retired namespace edge leaves scripts/namespace-governance-baseline.json. RAISE HISTORY, kept because the reasoning is the whole point of the file: Raised 2026-10-14 from 37176 to 38703 (+1527) because the growth is legitimate feature work spread across 56 commits, not one misplaced module — see the commit message for the analysis. Extraction was deliberately NOT chosen: audit.rs's four concerns (redaction, rate-limited write, hash chaining, off-device shipping) share a single insert_audit body whose docstring explains why a second writer would leak AUD-06's redacted keys. Raised again 2026-10-19 from 38703 to 39068 (+365), and the analysis is the same shape rather than a new judgement: 15 distinct files contributed net production growth across 952 commits, the largest single contributor is db/assignments.rs at 97 lines (27% of the delta) and the top three sum to 198 (54%), so there is no one misplaced module to extract — the growth is incremental work on assignments, provisioning, products CRUD, profile, sale deduction, CRL and tax assignments. Two caveats a reader should know before crediting this raise: the gate was RED for an unknown period before it was noticed (the doc pass that found it, docs/architecture/module-namespace-firewall.md, had itself been quoting the PREVIOUS ceiling of 37176), and a ceiling that is only ever moved after the fact is a changelog rather than a ratchet — the intended use is to move it deliberately as part of a change that also says why. NOTE: running verify-core-size.py --emit-baseline rewrites this description to a one-line default; if that happens, restore the history from git and re-append, which is exactly what this edit does. RAISE 39068 -> 39069 (2026-10-19, docs-auditor): exactly one production line, and it was forced by clippy rather than by new logic -- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` rejects the six-field sample-item tuple in crates/kasirmu-core/src/db/provisioning.rs with clippy::type_complexity, and the alias the lint asks for costs one declaration line. The alternative was measured and rejected: the struct form that would also have absorbed the ten sample literals adds roughly thirty lines, and the doc block was already cut from eight lines to three because comments are masked and do not count. So this +1 is the floor for this fix, not slack. The four-line cost is visible in `git diff 3cca800b6 -- crates/kasirmu-core/src/db/provisioning.rs` and nothing else in kasirmu-core/src changed since e087cc554 raised the previous ceiling (verified with `git diff --stat e087cc554..HEAD -- crates/kasirmu-core/src/`, one file). RAISE 39069 -> 40417 (2026-10-22): +1348 lines across debt optimization commits resolving todo-optimize-crates.md items: popularity batching (O-H01), chunked image batch queries (O-H02), concurrent location cache (O-M12), batched shortfall queries (O-M13), stock movement transaction chunking (O-M07), cached statements (O-L01), rollback logging (O-L02), store field encapsulation (O-L03), streaming CSV exports (O-L04), and indexed semantic pairing (O-L05). Measured across 178 production files. RAISE 40417 -> 40597 (2026-10-23): +180 production lines, all from the same lane's own commits, and the attribution is the point of recording it. Three contributors, in order: (1) the migrated-snapshot disk cache (ba3a605ac plus this round's extraction into crates/kasirmu-core/src/test_db_snapshot.rs, net +~200 lines across the two files) which took kasirmu-core's nextest run from 294.89 s to 48.52 s; (2) the per-database audit rate limiter (8dc23c42a, 5cd65971f, +94 lines in db/audit.rs) which ended a 20% test flake; (3) the scratch-fixture migration and its guard-threading, which is mostly test-only code the measure excludes. EXTRACTION WAS TRIED FIRST AND IS WORTH RECORDING: the cache was moved out of migrations.rs into its own module, which took that file from 972 to 867 lines against the 1000-line house rule — but it did NOT reduce the measured total, because the measure counts production lines across the whole of crates/kasirmu-core/src and the code still exists, just in a different file. So this raise is not a substitute for the extraction; it is the separate fact that the feature was added at all. A reader should also know that migrations.rs at 867 lines is still the largest single file in the crate and is the first place to look next time. RAISE 40597 -> 40616 (2026-10-24): +19 production lines, and the whole delta is attributable to TWO revisions after the ceiling was set -- verified rather than assumed, by re-measuring the tree at 7be89ae53 with this checker's own masker, which lands on exactly 40597 (so the baseline was NOT stale, and the entire +19 is post-baseline work). Per-file, net across 9 files: payment.rs +19 (24 -> 43), location_resolver.rs +3, and +1 each on sales_checkout.rs, sales_lifecycle.rs, rate_limiter.rs and sync_client/types.rs, against -5 on db/roles.rs, -1 on license_verification/crl.rs and -1 on migrations.rs. The largest single contributor is 100% of the net delta and it is PaymentSplitArg::effective_gateway_status (7116e47c1, the ADR-64 tender lifecycle state machine) -- a 24-line cohesive domain method with its own doc comment explaining Rules 1 and 3, and 58 lines of companion tests in payment_tests.rs. EXTRACTION WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED ON MEASUREMENT, and the reason is worth recording because it is the opposite of what an earlier note in this file's history assumed: splitting a file does NOT reduce this measure at all. The ceiling counts production lines across the whole of crates/kasirmu-core/src, so db/popularity.rs (834 masked lines, the crate's largest file) could be split into a submodule and the number would not move by one line. The only lever that lowers it is moving code OUT of the crate. There is no misplaced module here to move: the growth is one feature method plus incidental churn on eight other files, which is the same shape as the two raises already recorded above. Also corrected by this measurement: no file in the crate is over 1000 MASKED lines (popularity.rs is 834 masked against 1151 raw), so the 1000-line house rule was not in play either. ADR-67 SPLIT (2026-10-24): the crate is now graded on TWO budgets in addition to the whole-crate ceiling above, because measuring it as one number conflates two different questions. `db_ceiling` (27481) covers crates/kasirmu-core/src/db/ -- the crate's own `impl Store` surface, which cannot move out of the crate without moving the crate, measured at 67.7% of the whole -- and a rise there is SQL debt, not a modularity regression. `non_db_ceiling` (13135) covers everything else, which is the population Phase 3 P3.4's rule actually governs: the feature modules moved out to modules/, and this budget is what notices logic landing back. The three ceilings are independent and the two new ones partition TODAY's tree (27481 + 13135 = 40616); the whole-crate `ceiling` is left EXACTLY as it was so every historical raise above keeps its meaning, rather than being re-expressed in a new unit mid-history. See docs/decisions/2026-10-24-adr67-core-size-ratchet-measurement.md. Why this matters in one sentence: the whole-crate number was raised four times in five days (+1548 lines) and every raise was individually correct and correctly attributed, which is precisely the symptom of a ratchet measuring something it cannot influence.
measure: non-blank lines in crates/kasirmu-core/src production .rs files, minus inline #[cfg(test)] mod blocks
